# FIFA Men's and Women's World Cups: winners and hosts — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/fifa-world-cup.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/fifa-world-cup.ttl`](../decks/fifa-world-cup.ttl) · **Cards:** 64 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

The winner and the host country (or countries) of every FIFA World Cup, the men's tournament from 1930 to 2026 (23 tournaments) and the women's from 1991 to 2023 (9 tournaments): 64 cards. Front: the tournament and the question, e.g. "FIFA World Cup 1958: winner" or "FIFA Women's World Cup 2023: host"; back: the country in English and Swedish. Countries are named as they were at the time: "West Germany" for the titles of 1954, 1974 and 1990 and for the 1974 host. Results up to and including the 2026 men's World Cup, won by Spain on 19 July 2026. Taken from Wikidata and checked against FIFA's own data and the RSSSF.

## Licensing

The only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of tournaments, the winner and host of each, the English and Swedish names of the tournaments and countries, and the facts in the back notes (the 1950 final round, the 2026 final, the number of hosts and teams, West Germany's dates, England in the United Kingdom) come from it, so the deck can be CC0 1.0 like the rest of the library. FIFA's data API and the RSSSF pages (all rights reserved; RSSSF's permission to copy with acknowledgement is not a recognised open licence and is not relied on) and the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the Wikidata data gave and the names used at the time; no wording, table, data set or selection was copied from them. FIFA's terms limit use of its content and API to private, non-commercial use on FIFA's platforms (§5.3) and forbid using FIFA content, names, logos or marks without written agreement (§6.2): the API was consulted privately, and the deck reproduces nothing of FIFA's: no FIFA data, text, logo or mark, and no official tournament name (the fronts use Wikidata's aliases, e.g. "FIFA World Cup 1958"; the competition's name appears only to identify it). The provenance report cites FIFA's responses (tournament names as FIFA gives them, team ids, dates and scores) as short factual references so the checks can be repeated. The selection is every held edition of two competitions, the complete set, not a choice taken from any list. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence are not part of the CC0 deck: they remain under their sources' licences (Wikipedia text CC BY-SA 4.0 by Wikipedia contributors, each linked to the quoted revision; FIFA's data all rights reserved; each RSSSF page © its named author and RSSSF, credited in the sources) and are short quotations of at most one sentence each, given only to make the verification checkable.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with machine checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators; the deck is to be reviewed further by independent AI reviewers. The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. Finding the tournaments: the Wikidata items of the two competitions were found with the Wikidata search API (query 1): FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323). Query 2 selected every item whose P3450 (sports season of league or competition) is one of them, with start and end time (P580/P582), the truthy winner (P1346), country (P17) and the English and Swedish labels; the CSV was saved. Besides the tournaments it returned qualification groups, the unplayed 1942 and 1946 editions, future editions (2027 onward for women, 2030 onward for men) and the unofficial women's tournaments of 1970 and 1971.
3. Statements of all ranks: query 3 listed every P17, P276 and P1346 statement, with its rank, of the held editions 1930–2026. All are normal rank; every held edition has exactly one winner. Query 4 fetched the P17 and P1532 (country for sport) of the winning teams and of two locations, query 5 every English, Swedish and multilingual label and alias of the tournaments, teams and countries used, and query 6 the aliases of all the tournaments (the English "FIFA World Cup 1958" and Swedish "VM i fotboll 1958" forms on which the fronts are modelled).
4. The 2026 men's World Cup: the Wikidata item (Q5020214, fetched in full with query 7) gives the winner Spain (Q42267) without a reference, and its English description still read "being held". Because the tournament ended after the compiler's training data, the result was established from sources fetched on 2026-10-04: a web search for the final's result (news reports of Spain's 1–0 win over Argentina after extra time on 19 July 2026; discovery only, not cited; the exact search string of that first search was not recorded, and query 22 is the re-run made in QC round 3), then FIFA's own match data (query 8: the final of season 285023, Spain 1–0 Argentina, winner Spain), RSSSF's overview (query 10: "2026 Spain", "Spain 1-0 Argentina AET") and the Swedish Wikipedia introduction (query 12). Only the latter three are cited, as verification; the facts of the back note come from Wikidata's item of the final (Q55640701, query 17), which records the date, the teams, the 1–0 score, the winner and the goal in the second half of extra time.
5. Cross-check against FIFA: the script fifa_api.py (query 8, its source given in full) downloaded FIFA's public API list of seasons of competitions 17 (men) and 103 (women), each season's match list and the names of the host and winning teams, and printed each tournament's official name, host teams and final. For 1950, which had no final, the matches of the stage "Final Round" were listed (query 9). Every card was compared with this data: all 64 agree, under FIFA's own team names ("Germany FR", "Korea Republic", "USA", "China PR").
6. Cross-check against the RSSSF: the men's overview (query 10) gives the palmares, each final and the country of each final tournament; the women's overview and the RSSSF page of each Women's World Cup (query 11, rsssf_women.py, its source given in full; each page has its own author, credited in the source "rsssf-women-pages") give the palmares, the finals and in each page title the host. All 64 cards agree.
7. Team names as at the time: the cards name the winner and the host as the country the team or tournament represented at the time, the convention of FIFA's own records. For 1954, 1974 and 1990 the winner is West Germany (FIFA: "Germany FR", a team record of its own; RSSSF: "West Germany"), and the 1974 host is West Germany (FIFA's host team "Germany FR", although FIFA's tournament name is "1974 FIFA World Cup Germany"; RSSSF "[Final tournament in West Germany]"). Wikidata records these with the present-day items (the team Q43310, "Germany men's national association football team", and the country Germany, Q183); the West German names come from Wikidata's West Germany item (Q713750, en "West Germany", sv "Västtyskland") and the team's aliases "West Germany national football team" and "Västtysklands herrlandslag i fotboll". For 1966 the host is England, as FIFA ("1966 FIFA World Cup England™") and RSSSF name it; Wikidata's P17 is the United Kingdom (Q145), and the winner England comes from the team's P1532 (England, Q21). The West German name and dates of the notes come from Q713750 (its alias "Federal Republic of Germany (1949–1990)", P571, P576 and P1366); these checks confirm wording only. That the 1974 host was West Germany rests on FIFA's host team "Germany FR", RSSSF and the Swedish Wikipedia, not on a Wikidata statement. That West Germany won in 1954, 1974 and 1990 rests on the winner team of FIFA's final, "Germany FR", and on RSSSF ("West Germany"), not on a Wikidata statement (Wikidata has only the team's alias); the Swedish Wikipedia confirms the Swedish name (for 1974 its introduction gives the host only, and its infobox "Mästare" the winner).
8. English and Swedish text: the fronts are the compiler's own pattern "FIFA World Cup 1958: winner" / "VM i fotboll 1958: segrare" (host: "värdland"), and "FIFA Women's World Cup 2023: …" / "VM i fotboll för damer 2023: …", built from Wikidata's aliases of the tournaments (for those without such an alias the builder checks the label instead; see the checks). The backs are the English and Swedish Wikidata labels of the countries, except "China" (Wikidata's English label is "People's Republic of China"; the Swedish label is "Kina") and "West Germany" (see above). The United States is "USA" in Swedish (Wikidata's Swedish label). Several hosts are joined with "and"/"och" in FIFA's order (South Korea and Japan; Australia and New Zealand), the 2026 hosts in alphabetical order (Canada, Mexico and the United States / Kanada, Mexiko och USA, as on the Swedish Wikipedia).
9. Swedish check: the script svwiki.py (query 12, its source given in full) fetched, through the MediaWiki API, the introductions and current revision ids of the Swedish Wikipedia articles on the tournaments with a convention or a note; the quoted sentences, linked to their revisions, are in the cards' evidence ("Turneringen vanns av Västtyskland", "spelades i England", "arrangerades i Västtyskland", "spelades i Kina" …).
10. Notes: a back note in the compiler's own words was added only where it helps to answer or to avoid a wrong answer, and only with facts that Wikidata (the content source) gives, the verification sources confirming them: 1950 (no final; Uruguay won the four-team final round, Q989777, whose last match Uruguay v Brazil, Q754483, ended 2–1 on 16 July 1950; query 16), West Germany (1954, 1974 and 1990 winners, 1974 host: the Federal Republic of Germany of 1949–1990, Q713750), England as a country of the United Kingdom (1966, Q21 P31 Q3336843), the first World Cup with two hosts (2002) and the first with three hosts and 48 teams (2026), both from the count of P17 values and the P1132 of every edition (query 15), and the 2026 final (Q55640701). The first version also had notes with FIFA's names ("Germany FR", "1974 FIFA World Cup Germany", "2002 FIFA World Cup Korea/Japan") and the move of the 2003 Women's World Cup from China because of SARS; these rested on verification sources only and were removed in QC round 3. Each note's facts are in the evidence of its card.
11. Assembly: the throwaway helper script make_dossier.py (kept only in the compiler's scratch directory, not part of the record) built the cards from the saved responses, asserting for each card that the Wikidata winner and host, FIFA's final and host teams and RSSSF's palmares and host agree with the card, so a disagreement stops the build. The dossier's text (sources, method, selection, licensing) was written with a second throwaway helper, meta.py. Their Wikidata assertions are re-run by the builder's checks on every build; their FIFA and RSSSF comparisons are recorded card by card in the evidence and were repeated independently in QC rounds 1 and 3. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish front wording (an alias or the label of the tournament), the winner (P1346) or host (P17; for 2007 women the P276 location and its P17), the team's P1532 country for sport, and the English and Swedish labels of the country on the back. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).
12. Review: three independent AI reviewers (Claude) checked the deck for factual accuracy, for language and language tags, and for licensing and documentation (QC rounds 1–3). The changes they led to (the title and description wording, the notes rebuilt on Wikidata facts, the RSSSF authors, the full FIFA terms, the scripts given in full, the shorter quotations) were made by the authoring agent and re-checked with the builder's Wikidata checks and the validators. No human subject expert has reviewed the cards.

## Selection

Every FIFA World Cup actually held from the first (Uruguay 1930) to the most recent (Canada, Mexico and the United States 2026), 23 tournaments, and every FIFA Women's World Cup from the first (China 1991) to the most recent (Australia and New Zealand 2023), 9 tournaments; two cards for each, the winner and the host country or countries: 64 cards. Left out: the World Cups of 1942 and 1946, which were not held; the unofficial women's tournaments of 1970 (Italy) and 1971 (Mexico), which were not organised by FIFA and are in Wikidata only as editions of Q19323 (RSSSF lists them among the unofficial tournaments before FIFA's first in 1991); the 2027 Women's World Cup (Brazil, June–July 2027) and all later tournaments, not yet played; qualification tournaments; runners-up, scores, venues and individual awards. The host card names countries, not cities or stadiums. Results are as of 2026-10-04.

## Queries

**1. Find the items of the two competitions (wbsearchentities)** (Wikidata: the editions of the FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323), their winners (P1346), countries (P17), locations (P276) and numbers of participants (P1132), the national teams' country for sport (P1532), the 1950 final round (Q989777) and its match Uruguay v Brazil (Q754483), the 2026 final (Q55640701), West Germany (Q713750), and the labels of the tournaments and countries)

```
curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=FIFA%20World%20Cup&language=en&limit=10&format=json"
curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?action=wbsearchentities&search=FIFA%20Women%27s%20World%20Cup&language=en&limit=3&format=json"
```

**2. Every edition (P3450) of both competitions with start/end, truthy winner, country and labels (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q1.rq -o q1.csv https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [saved as q1.rq]** (Wikidata: the editions of the FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323), their winners (P1346), countries (P17), locations (P276) and numbers of participants (P1132), the national teams' country for sport (P1532), the 1950 final round (Q989777) and its match Uruguay v Brazil (Q754483), the 2026 final (Q55640701), West Germany (Q713750), and the labels of the tournaments and countries)

```
SELECT ?ed ?series ?edEn ?edSv ?start ?end ?winner ?winnerEn ?winnerSv ?country ?countryEn ?countrySv WHERE {
  VALUES ?series { wd:Q19317 wd:Q19323 }
  ?ed wdt:P3450 ?series .
  OPTIONAL { ?ed wdt:P580 ?start }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed wdt:P582 ?end }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed wdt:P1346 ?winner .
    OPTIONAL { ?winner rdfs:label ?winnerEn FILTER(LANG(?winnerEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?winner rdfs:label ?winnerSv FILTER(LANG(?winnerSv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed wdt:P17 ?country .
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countryEn FILTER(LANG(?countryEn) = "en") }
    OPTIONAL { ?country rdfs:label ?countrySv FILTER(LANG(?countrySv) = "sv") } }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed rdfs:label ?edEn FILTER(LANG(?edEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed rdfs:label ?edSv FILTER(LANG(?edSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?series ?start ?ed
```

**3. Every P17, P276 and P1346 statement, with its rank, of the editions held 1930–2026 (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q2.rq -o q2.csv https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [saved as q2.rq]** (Wikidata: the editions of the FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323), their winners (P1346), countries (P17), locations (P276) and numbers of participants (P1132), the national teams' country for sport (P1532), the 1950 final round (Q989777) and its match Uruguay v Brazil (Q754483), the 2026 final (Q55640701), West Germany (Q713750), and the labels of the tournaments and countries)

```
SELECT ?ed ?edEn ?prop ?rank ?val ?valEn ?valSv WHERE {
  VALUES ?series { wd:Q19317 wd:Q19323 }
  ?ed wdt:P3450 ?series ; wdt:P580 ?start .
  FILTER(YEAR(?start) >= 1930 && YEAR(?start) <= 2026)
  ?ed wdt:P31 ?class .
  VALUES (?prop ?p ?ps) { ("P17" p:P17 ps:P17) ("P276" p:P276 ps:P276) ("P1346" p:P1346 ps:P1346) }
  ?ed ?p ?st . ?st ?ps ?val ; wikibase:rank ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valEn FILTER(LANG(?valEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valSv FILTER(LANG(?valSv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?ed rdfs:label ?edEn FILTER(LANG(?edEn) = "en") }
}
ORDER BY ?start ?prop
```

**4. P17 and P1532 (country for sport) of the winning teams and of Shanghai and Guangzhou (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q3.rq -o q3.csv https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [saved as q3.rq]** (Wikidata: the editions of the FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323), their winners (P1346), countries (P17), locations (P276) and numbers of participants (P1132), the national teams' country for sport (P1532), the 1950 final round (Q989777) and its match Uruguay v Brazil (Q754483), the 2026 final (Q55640701), West Germany (Q713750), and the labels of the tournaments and countries)

```
SELECT ?item ?prop ?val ?valEn ?valSv WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q134916 wd:Q676899 wd:Q43310 wd:Q83459 wd:Q47762 wd:Q79800 wd:Q47774 wd:Q42267
                 wd:Q334526 wd:Q751994 wd:Q154408 wd:Q388232 wd:Q847623 wd:Q8686 wd:Q16572 }
  VALUES ?prop { wdt:P17 wdt:P1532 }
  ?item ?prop ?val .
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valEn FILTER(LANG(?valEn) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?val rdfs:label ?valSv FILTER(LANG(?valSv) = "sv") }
}
ORDER BY ?item
```

**5. English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases of the countries, teams and some tournaments (curl -s -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -H "Accept: text/csv" --data-urlencode query@q4.rq -o q4.csv https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) [saved as q4.rq]** (Wikidata: the editions of the FIFA World Cup (Q19317) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (Q19323), their winners (P1346), countries (P17), locations (P276) and numbers of participants (P1132), the national teams' country for sport (P1532), the 1950 final round (Q989777) and its match Uruguay v Brazil (Q754483), the 2026 final (Q55640701), West Germany (Q713750), and the labels of the tournaments and countries)

```
SELECT ?item ?kind ?lang ?text WHERE {
  VALUES ?item { wd:Q43310 wd:Q47762 wd:Q713750 wd:Q21 wd:Q183 wd:Q77 wd:Q38 wd:Q142 wd:Q155 wd:Q39 wd:Q34 wd:Q298
                 wd:Q145 wd:Q96 wd:Q414 wd:Q29 wd:Q30 wd:Q884 wd:Q17 wd:Q258 wd:Q159 wd:Q846 wd:Q16 wd:Q148 wd:Q408
                 wd:Q664 wd:Q20 wd:Q166121 wd:Q134202 wd:Q367805 wd:Q459419 wd:Q132529 wd:Q131075 wd:Q47735 wd:Q5020214 wd:Q19672232 }
  VALUES ?lang { "en" "sv" "mul" }
  { ?item rdfs:label ?text BIND("label" AS ?kind) } UNION { ?item skos:altLabel ?text BIND("alias" AS ?kind) }
  FILTER(LANG(?text) = ?lang)

**8. fifa_api.py, run as "python3 fifa_api.py": the seasons, host teams, matches and finals of competitions 17 and 103 (each response saved under fifa/). Seasons fetched: competition 17: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 15, 21, 26, 32, 39, 50, 59, 68, 76, 84, 1013, 4395, 9741, 249715, 251164, 254645, 255711, 285023; competition 103: 3373, 4654, 4644, 6929, 10232, 251475, 266030, 278513, 285026, 289120. Source of the script:** (FIFA's public data API (api.fifa.com v3): the seasons of the FIFA World Cup (competition 17) and the FIFA Women's World Cup (competition 103), their host teams and their matches)

```
"""Fetch the FIFA World Cup and Women's World Cup seasons, their final matches and host teams from FIFA's public API.

Saves every raw response under ./fifa/ and prints a summary table.
"""
import json
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = HERE / "fifa"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
API = "https://api.fifa.com/api/v3"


def get(url: str, name: str) -> dict:
    path = OUT / name
    if path.exists():
        return json.loads(path.read_text())
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        data = r.read()
    path.write_bytes(data)
    time.sleep(0.3)
    return json.loads(data)


def name(x):
    return x[0]["Description"] if x else ""


team_names: dict[str, str] = {}


def team(tid: str) -> str:
    if tid not in team_names:
        t = get(f"{API}/teams/{tid}?language=en", f"team-{tid}.json")
        team_names[tid] = name(t.get("Name", []))
    return team_names[tid]


for comp in ("17", "103"):
    seasons = get(f"{API}/seasons?idCompetition={comp}&count=100&language=en", f"seasons-{comp}.json")["Results"]
    for s in sorted(seasons, key=lambda s: s["StartDate"]):
        sid = s["IdSeason"]
        hosts = [team(h["IdTeam"]) for h in s.get("HostTeams") or []]
        matches = get(f"{API}/calendar/matches?idCompetition={comp}&idSeason={sid}&count=500&language=en",
                      f"matches-{comp}-{sid}.json")["Results"]
        finals = [m for m in matches if name(m.get("StageName", [])).lower() == "final"]
        if finals:
            m = finals[-1]
            h, a = m["Home"], m["Away"]
            win = m.get("Winner")
            wname = team(win) if win else ""
            line = (f"{name(h.get('TeamName', []))} {m.get('HomeTeamScore')}-{m.get('AwayTeamScore')} "
                    f"{name(a.get('TeamName', []))} (pens {m.get('HomeTeamPenaltyScore')}-{m.get('AwayTeamPenaltyScore')}) "
                    f"{m.get('Date')} winner={wname} stadium={name((m.get('Stadium') or {}).get('Name', []))}")
        else:
            stages = sorted({name(m.get("StageName", [])) for m in matches})
            line = f"NO FINAL; stages {stages}; {len(matches)} matches"
        print(comp, sid, name(s["Name"]), "| hosts:", hosts, "|", line)

```

"""Download RSSSF's page for each FIFA Women's World Cup 1991-2023 and print its title and first heading lines."""
import html
import re
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
for f in ["wwc91f", "wwc95f", "wwc99f", "wwc03f", "wwc07f", "wwc2011f", "wwc2015f", "wwc2019f", "wwc2023f"]:
    url = f"https://www.rsssf.org/tablesw/{f}.html"
    path = HERE / f"rsssf-{f}.html"
    if not path.exists():
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
            path.write_bytes(r.read())
        time.sleep(1)
    t = path.read_text(encoding="latin-1")
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", t, re.I | re.S)
    body = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", t))
    lines = [l.strip() for l in body.splitlines() if l.strip()][:4]
    print(url, "|", title.group(1).strip() if title else "", "|", " / ".join(lines))

```

```
"""Fetch the introductions (plain text) and current revision ids of Swedish Wikipedia articles via the MediaWiki API."""
import json
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
TITLES = [
    "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 1954", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 1966", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 1974",
    "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 1990", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 2002", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll 2026",
    "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll för damer 1991", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll för damer 2003",
    "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll för damer 2007", "Världsmästerskapet i fotboll för damer 2023",
]
out = {}
for t in TITLES:
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"action": "query", "prop": "extracts|revisions", "exintro": 1, "explaintext": 1,
                                "rvprop": "ids", "titles": t, "format": "json", "formatversion": 2, "redirects": 1})
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?{q}", headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        page = json.load(r)["query"]["pages"][0]
    out[t] = {"revid": page.get("revisions", [{}])[0].get("revid"), "intro": page.get("extract", "")}
    print("==", t, out[t]["revid"])
    print(out[t]["intro"][:700])
(HERE / "svwiki.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 29 findings: 25 fixed, 1 rejected after checking, 3 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (402 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's winner and host against Wikidata, FIFA's own data and the RSSSF; the Swedish names against Wikidata labels and the Swedish Wikipedia; the 2026 result against sources fetched on the day. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 64 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

Wikidata, FIFA and RSSSF agree on the winner and the host of all 32 tournaments (make_dossier.py asserts it for every card). The discrepancies are in naming: Wikidata records West Germany's titles and the 1974 host with present-day items and the 1966 host as the United Kingdom, while FIFA and RSSSF name West Germany and England; the cards follow FIFA's records and check the Wikidata items and aliases that carry these names. No Wikidata check was skipped because Wikidata disagreed; one English label check was left out where Wikidata has no matching text (China).

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| men-2026-winner | The tournament ended on 19 July 2026, after the compiler's training data; Wikidata's P1346 (Spain) has no reference and the item's English description still says "being held". | Result confirmed on 2026-10-04 from FIFA's match data (final of season 285023: Spain 1–0 Argentina, winner Spain), RSSSF ("2026 Spain", "Spain 1-0 Argentina AET", page updated 21 Sep 2026) and the Swedish Wikipedia; a web search found news reports (NPR) of the same result. The back note gives the final. | no change needed |
| men-1954-winner | Wikidata's winner is Q43310, labelled "Germany men's national association football team" (country for sport Q183, Germany); FIFA records the team as "Germany FR" (team id 44023, distinct from "Germany", 43948) and RSSSF as "West Germany". The same holds for 1974 and 1990. | Back "West Germany" / "Västtyskland", the name at the time; checks the P1346 link, Q43310's aliases "West Germany national football team" / "Västtysklands herrlandslag i fotboll" and Q713750's labels. A note explains the name. 2014's winner is "Germany" / "Tyskland". | fixed |

(Note rewritten in QC round 3 from Wikidata's Q713750; FIFA's tournament name no longer given.) | fixed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 64 cards, their notes and the Wikidata checks, against RSSSF, English Wikipedia, news reports of the 2026 final and live Wikidata.

No factual errors in any of the 64 cards; the builder's Wikidata checks passed. Two documentation suggestions, both applied.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| men-1974-host | Two of the Wikidata checks (Q183's alias "Federal Republic of Germany" and Q713750's labels) do not link the 1974 edition to West Germany; only P17 = Q183 is tied to the edition. The same wording point applies to the 1954 and 1990 winner cards. | Verified: Q166121 has only P17 Q183, and nothing links it to Q713750. The card's Wikidata evidence and method step 7 now say that the Q713750 checks confirm wording only and that the West Germany host rests on FIFA (host team "Germany FR"), RSSSF and the Swedish Wikipedia; the same sentence is in the evidence of the 1954, 1974 and 1990 winner cards. The 1974 host card's checks now include Q713750's alias "Federal Republic of Germany (1949–1990)" and dates, for the rebuilt note (round 3). | fixed |
